summary.headline: HEGAM Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue from continuing operations rose to INR430 crores (vs INR176 crores), with EBITDA margin of 57%, aided by one-time power-segment income.
summary.overview: Q2 FY27 is the first quarter post-demerger of graphite business from HEG Limited, with FY26 comparatives restated to exclude it. Continuing-operations revenue was INR430 crores vs INR176 crores a year ago, EBITDA INR313 crores (57% margin) and PAT INR209 crores vs INR69 crores. Management said part of the Power segment's income was one-time (about 40% of its Q2 segment EBIT, per management), so the margin is not a run-rate figure. The call focused on the INR5,500 crore expansion plan (anode to 44,000 t, graphene 500 t, crucibles, RePlus 6 GWh), with the anode commissioning timeline of June 2027 and a steady-state group revenue guide of INR7,500-8,200 crores.

segments.name: Power (hydro and wind, IPP)
segments.commentary: Segment revenue about INR212 crores in Q2 (up 15% QoQ) and segment EBIT about INR190 crores (up 64%). Management said about 40% of the EBIT was one-time (transmission-line ISTS arrears and insurance gain) and about 60% recurring. Normative output about 1,000 MU a year, 75:25 H1:H2 split; PLF 43-44%; merchant realisation about INR6-6.5/unit this year.

segments.name: Anode (TACC)
segments.commentary: Phase 1 20,000 t Dewas plant 61% complete, commercial commissioning targeted June 2027, first-year utilisation assumed at 35%. Phase 2 takes total capacity to 44,000 t by March 2029. Management guides anode EBITDA margin 28-33%, rising to above 35% with crucible backward integration.

segments.name: Graphene (TACC)
segments.commentary: 10 t pilot plant running. Commercial plant of 500 t targeted by September 2028 (first 200 t on this timeline, a further 300 t delayed pending land and environmental permissions). About 90 t of orders and LOIs in hand; management guides EBITDA margin above 40-45%.

segments.name: RePlus Engitech (BESS / EV)
segments.commentary: Capacity expanding from 1 GWh to 6 GWh; INR250 crores capex spent so far on the expansion; about 1.5-2 GWh in active execution. Management guides EBITDA around 10% (plus or minus 1-2%); about 70-80% of current business is EPC, shifting to 50:50 next year.

segments.name: Graphite electrodes (HEG Limited, demerged)
segments.commentary: Revenue fell about 20-23% QoQ per an analyst question; management deferred detail to a separate graphite electrode call about a week after Diwali. HEG Graphite listing expected around the third week of November 2026.

guidance_outlook: Total group capex (anode Phase 1 and 2, RePlus expansion, crucible, graphene) about INR5,500 crores: about INR2,300 crores in FY27, INR1,600-1,700 crores in FY28, balance in FY29.
Steady-state (FY29-30) group revenue about INR7,500-8,200 crores, with group EBITDA margin of 25-28%.

Anode EBITDA margin above 35% expected after backward integration into crucibles; average anode cost cited at about INR9 lakh/t blended (INR11 lakh/t on first 20,000 t, INR6 lakh/t on the next 24,000 t).
Proposed 300 MW standalone C&I solar project (capex about INR1,200 crores, expected in about 12 months) is not in the capex figure because it is not yet signed; management cited double-digit IRR.
Management said ROCE is expected above 20-25% across businesses, with government incentives to be discussed soon.
risks_watch: Q2 EBITDA and PAT include one-time Power segment income (about 40% of Power EBIT); Q3 and Q4 run-rate will be lower.
Execution risk: Dewas anode Phase 1 is 61% complete, with first-year utilisation assumed at 35%; ramp to 90% is unproven.
Customer contracts are on a no-name basis and many are LOIs/MOUs rather than signed orders; 3-4 LOIs signed, 90 t graphene orders/LOIs.
Graphene 300 t additional capacity delayed pending land and environmental permissions.
Competition from China and other players as margins attract entry; management could not say whether peers will backward integrate.
Power prices are merchant and volatile; management's INR350 crore power EBITDA guidance assumes lower prices than current INR6-6.5/unit.
Cash upstreaming between HEGAM subsidiaries and the Statkraft-linked debt remain open; a plan is to come in a few quarters.
Graphite electrode business decline (about 20-23% QoQ per analyst) to be explained on a separate call after Diwali; HEG Graphite listing expected around the third week of November 2026.
Government subsidy and incentive announcements are pending and included in ROCE expectations.
summary.management_tone: Confident and expansive on growth and customer demand, with specific numbers on capex and margins. Management was evasive on the graphite electrode decline and on RePlus pricing (deferring to a separate call or saying figures are sensitive), and on cash upstreaming (asking for a few quarters). Several answers were qualitative or deferred.

qa_highlights.question: What is the total capex for all the expansions and how is it broken up?
qa_highlights.answer: Total about INR5,500 crores including 20,000 t existing (about INR2,350 crores), 24,000 t additional (about INR1,600 crores), graphene INR500 crores, crucible INR475 crores, RePlus expansion INR250 crores spent and INR230 crores for a Gujarat BESS IPP project.

qa_highlights.question: How is capex phased by year and what is the EBITDA margin outlook for each business?
qa_highlights.answer: About INR2,300 crores in FY27, INR1,600-1,700 crores in FY28, balance in FY29. Anode EBITDA 28-33% rising above 35% with crucible integration; graphene above 45%; RePlus around 10%.

qa_highlights.question: Are there confirmed orders for the planned capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: Chairman said contracts are on a no-name basis, with 3-4 LOIs signed and 3-4 more expected in months; customer demand led the move from 20,000 t to 44,000 t; Dewas site capped at 44,000 t.

qa_highlights.question: What is the ramp-up plan for anode capacity?
qa_highlights.answer: First-year utilisation assumed at 35% because it is a large construction plant; management said ramp from 50% to 90% is not a problem given linear equipment; first 20,000 t mostly exports.

qa_highlights.question: Why was the power segment EBIT margin so high in Q2 and how much is one-time?
qa_highlights.answer: Higher one-time receipts in Q2 (transmission-line ISTS arrears, insurance gain); about 40% of the INR190 crores Power EBIT is one-time and about 60% recurring, so the 40% will not recur in Q3 and Q4.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the solar project and the hydro plans?
qa_highlights.answer: A 300 MW standalone C&I solar project at about INR1,200 crores, around 12 months from completion, not yet signed so excluded from capex; management cited double-digit IRR. Management said it is not pursuing many more C&I projects.

qa_highlights.question: Can cash be upstreamed between subsidiaries given the Statkraft-linked debt?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is evaluating options to consolidate the power business and deploy cash, but asked for a few quarters before updating.

capex_capacity: Total capex across anode (20,000 t Dewas Phase 1 plus 24,000 t Phase 2), RePlus expansion, crucible and graphene is about INR5,500 crores; current 20,000 t anode capex about INR2,350 crores, additional 24,000 t about INR1,600 crores, graphene INR500 crores, crucible (80,000 units) INR475 crores, RePlus 1 GWh to 6 GWh INR250 crores spent so far, plus INR230 crores on a BESS IPP project in Gujarat.
Phased capex: about INR2,300 crores in FY27, INR1,600-1,700 crores in FY28, balance in FY29. Capex of about INR490 crores in H1 FY27, largely anode.

Dewas Phase 1 (20,000 t) 61% complete, commercial commissioning targeted June 2027; Phase 2 takes capacity to 44,000 t by March 2029 on the same 105-acre site; management said 60,000 t was the site's preferred limit but 44,000 t is the maximum fit.

Graphene: 10 t pilot running; 500 t commercial plant targeted by September 2028 in a new location, split into 200 t (already started) and 300 t delayed pending land and environmental permissions; graphene asset turn about 1:1, anode about 0.8x.

Proposed 300 MW standalone C&I solar project at about INR1,200 crores, expected in about 12 months, excluded from capex as it is not yet signed; RePlus 5 GWh capacity COD cited as March 2027 by the RePlus CEO.
demand_pricing: Management cited global Li-ion battery production rising from about 3 TWh in 2026 to 8 TWh by 2035, and graphite anode demand from about 2.9 million t to 8 million t over the same period; non-China anode demand projected above 1 million t by 2030.

Anode: over 100,000 t of customer MOUs in advanced discussions; 3-4 LOIs signed and 3-4 more expected in the next few months; contracts on a no-name basis. Customers include non-Chinese cell makers in Korea, Japan, US, Germany and Middle East.

Anode raw material: green petroleum coke and power make up more than 60% of cost; main suppliers from US, UK and Japan. Average anode cost about INR9 lakh/t blended (INR11 lakh/t on first 20,000 t, INR6 lakh/t on next 24,000 t). First 20,000 t mostly for export.
Graphene: about 90 t of orders and LOIs; management guides EBITDA margin of 40-45% and said no pricing disclosed; first 90 t supply to start in H2 FY28.

Power: normative about 1,000 MU/yr, 75:25 H1:H2 split; PLF 43-44%; merchant realisation about INR6-6.5/unit this year; peaking power about 30% of output at around INR9-10/unit; management guides power EBITDA of INR350 crores on lower prices.
RePlus: EBITDA around 10% (plus or minus 1-2%); 70-80% of business is EPC and 20-30% manufacturing and supply, moving to 50:50 next year and about 20% EPC in two years.
Crucible: about 40% cheaper than imports per management; external crucible realisation and margins guided at around 30-40%; in-house need peaks at 40,000-45,000 t.

Competition: China is sole crucible producer today; management said the company was ahead of other Indian anode entrants given 12-18 month qualification cycles. Graphite electrode revenue fell about 20-23% QoQ per an analyst, deferred to a separate call.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Q2 EBITDA margin of 57% is inflated by one-time Power income (about 40% of INR190 crore Power EBIT), so Q3-Q4 run-rate margin falls; margin expands only as anode ramps and crucible integration lifts anode margin above 35%, guided steady-state group EBITDA 25-28% for FY29-30.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Dewas anode Phase 1 of 20,000 t is 61% complete with commercial commissioning targeted June 2027, and RePlus is moving from 1 GWh to 6 GWh with INR250 crore already spent and 1.5-2 GWh in active execution.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Anode first-year utilisation assumed at 35% on 20,000 t from June 2027 and graphene first 90 t supply starts H2 FY28, though the ramp to 90% is unproven and 300 t of graphene is delayed.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Capex is already committed at about INR5,500 crore with INR2,300 crore in FY27, and a 300 MW standalone C&I solar project at about INR1,200 crore is proposed but not yet signed, so a new announcement depends on signing it and on the Gujarat BESS IPP.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Management guided anode utilisation at a deliberately humble 35% and said 100,000 t of MOUs are in advanced talks, so upside exists if LOIs convert, but only 3-4 LOIs are signed so far.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: About 40% of Q2 Power EBIT was one-time (ISTS arrears and insurance gain), management's power EBITDA guide of INR350 crore assumes lower merchant prices than the current INR6-6.5/unit, and the graphene 300 t tranche is delayed pending land and environmental permissions.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Graphene first 90 t supply to start in H2 FY28 against about 90 t of orders and LOIs, and crucible (80,000 units, INR475 crore) is approved to move into integration with anode.

rows.label: Anode customer MOUs and LOIs convert to contracts
rows.why: Over 100,000 t of customer MOUs are in advanced discussion and 3-4 LOIs are signed with 3-4 more expected, but contracts are no-name and not yet firm orders.

rows.label: Cash upstreaming and Statkraft-linked debt plan
rows.why: Cash of INR1,300 crore against long-term borrowings of INR1,036 crore gives net cash on a cash-to-borrowing basis, but management asked for a few quarters before a plan to consolidate Power and deploy cash.

rows.label: Government incentives and subsidy announcements
rows.why: Management said government incentives will be discussed soon and ROCE above 20-25% expectations depend on them, but no amount or approval has been disclosed.
